title: Service, Action, Creativity: Balance the CAS Strands
summary: Balance creativity, activity and service in IB CAS from September to November with a realistic weekly plan, project ideas and portfolio advice.
body_markdown:
Balancing the three CAS strands does not mean dividing every week or hour into equal thirds. The IB requires a **reasonable balance** of Creativity, Activity and Service across a CAS programme that continues regularly for at least **18 months** . Schools may set more specific expectations, but the official framework emphasizes sustained engagement, meaningful learning and evidence rather than a universal hourly quota.


From September to November, choose repeatable experiences, keep all three strands visible and begin planning your collaborative CAS project.


### First, it is Activity rather than Action


Some students still refer to **Creativity, Action, Service** because this wording appears in older resources. The current official term is **Creativity, Activity, Service** , abbreviated to **CAS** .


The[official IB overview of CAS](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/creativity-activity-and-service/) defines the strands as follows:


Strand Official meaning in practice Suitable fall-term examples


**Creativity** Exploring and extending ideas toward an original or interpretive product or performance Photography, music, design or writing


**Activity** Physical exertion that contributes to a healthy lifestyle Running, dance, hiking or fitness training


**Service** Collaborative and reciprocal engagement with a community in response to an authentic need Tutoring, environmental work or community support


Creativity is not restricted to fine art, and Activity does not require competitive sport. Service is more than completing helpful tasks. It should respond to a genuine need while respecting the community's perspectives and autonomy.


### What a reasonable balance actually means


The IB does not require exactly one-third of your time in each strand. A portfolio can be stronger in one area during a particular month while remaining balanced across the complete programme.


Cross-country training might make Activity dominant in September and October. You could maintain balance through a weekly creative commitment and a service experience that becomes more substantial later. What matters is authentic, sustained engagement with every strand.


One experience can cover multiple strands. Designing accessible reading resources may combine Creativity and Service, while organizing a community fitness event may combine Activity and Service. Apply only labels that accurately reflect what you did.


### A September-to-November CAS plan


Choose a small number of **anchor experiences** that can continue during tests, coursework deadlines and busy school weeks.


Period Main priority Practical action


**September** Establish the three-strand baseline Select repeatable experiences, confirm approval requirements and set initial goals


**October** Test sustainability Continue your anchors, record evidence and replace unreliable experiences


**November** Review balance and project readiness Audit the strands, check learning outcomes and agree on a project plan


A manageable week might contain one Activity session, one alternating Creativity or Service block and a **10-15 minute** documentation session. This is more sustainable than leaving reflections until the end of the month. See RevisionDojo's advice on[balancing CAS with academics and social life](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-balance-cas-with-academics-and-social-life) for additional scheduling strategies.


### Use anchor experiences instead of chasing equal hours


An anchor experience is predictable, repeatable and easy to document, such as orchestra rehearsal, regular running or weekly tutoring.


Choose anchors using four questions:


- Can I continue this during a demanding assessment week?
- Does it involve genuine challenge, growth or responsibility?
- Can I collect evidence without invading anyone's privacy?
- Will I have meaningful decisions or difficulties to reflect upon?


This produces better evidence of commitment than unrelated one-off events. The[RevisionDojo overview of succeeding in IB CAS](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-excel-in-the-ibdp-cas-program-creativity-activity-service) explains how sustained commitments support a balanced programme.


### Start the CAS project during the fall term


Every student must participate in at least one **CAS project** . According to the[IB's CAS project guidance](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/dp-core/creativity-activity-and-service/cas-projects/) , it is collaborative, consists of sequential CAS experiences and lasts at least **one month** from planning through completion. It may address one, two or all three strands.


September-to-November is a useful planning window for investigating a need, finding collaborators and revising unrealistic ideas. Possible projects include an accessible community arts event, a sustained environmental campaign or physical activity sessions for younger students.


A project is not simply a long experience. Collaboration, intentional planning and a connected sequence of work are essential. Review the[difference between a CAS project and a CAS experience](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-counts-as-a-cas-project-vs-a-cas-experience) before recording it.


### Track learning, not just participation


CAS is not formally graded, but successful completion is compulsory for the IB Diploma. The official[CAS subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/cas-2016-english-1st-final-web.pdf) requires portfolio evidence of achieving **seven learning outcomes** , including challenge, planning, commitment, collaboration and ethical choices.


After an experience, save one relevant artifact and write a focused reflection. Explain a specific difficulty or decision, what it revealed and what you will change. Evidence could include a photograph, draft, training record, agenda or feedback collected with consent.


Do not claim every learning outcome after every session. Select only outcomes genuinely demonstrated by the evidence. RevisionDojo's guide to[writing stronger CAS reflections](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-cas-reflections-what-coordinators-want) explains how to move from description to analysis.


### Common mistakes during the fall term


Treating balance as a mathematical quota encourages superficial experiences chosen only to fill categories. Overcommitting in September is equally risky because abandoned commitments provide weak evidence of perseverance.


Other common problems include:


- counting an ordinary routine without establishing purpose, challenge or growth
- assuming paid work or a required course task automatically qualifies
- designing service without consulting the community concerned
- attaching strand labels that the experience cannot support
- postponing evidence and reflection until details are forgotten


Ask your CAS coordinator to confirm that an experience meets your school's expectations. Schools implement the IB framework locally and may require specific forms, deadlines, supervisors or portfolio conventions. RevisionDojo's[CAS minimum requirements guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/understanding-the-minimum-requirements-for-cas-in-the-ibdp) can help you prepare questions, but your coordinator makes school-level decisions.


### Conclusion


To balance Service, Activity and Creativity, maintain meaningful engagement in every strand without forcing exact weekly equality. Use September to establish sustainable anchors, October to test them and November to review your portfolio and advance the CAS project.


Consistency, honest reflection and purposeful choices matter more than accumulating activities. RevisionDojo's CAS guides can support your planning, while Study Notes, Questionbank and Jojo AI can help protect the academic study time that CAS should complement.
